statement: Eight memory shires, four on the west side (0-3) and four on the east side (4-7) of the die, each driving two 16-bit LPDDR4X channels: 16 channels in all.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.17 §1.5 (txt line 544-548); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7 and §7.1
note: West 0-3 / east 4-7 is the PRM's and the firmware's naming; the latency fit's logical map draws them above and below the grid (chip-diagram fact fw.memshires).

statement: Four LPDDR4X packages on the card, each with four 16-bit channels (64 bits per package, 256 bits in all); two memory shires share each package.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.17 §1.5; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7 ('Two Memshires communicate with each 64-bit LPDDR4X memory device'); external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf pdf p.3 ('4 x LPDDR4x DRAM devices for a combined 256-bit memory interface')
note: The datasheet's §2.2.2 (pdf p.16) calls each package a 'bank' ('four banks of LPDDR4X memory. Each bank is controlled by two Memory Shires'): not a DRAM bank. The diagram should say 'package'.

statement: Which two memory shires share each LPDDR4X package is not documented; the chip diagram pairs neighbours (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) on an assumption.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7; docs/reports/data/2026-09-27-chip-diagram/facts.json facts['dram.pkg-pairing']; hub ask 'ask-card-schematic' (docs/reports/sources/limits-of-observability.data.json improvements[24])

statement: Each memory shire holds two Synopsys uMCTL2 DDR controller instances, one per 16-bit channel: the firmware programs controller blocks 0 and 1 of every memory shire, and the memory shire has separate mode-register read-back registers for 'memory controller 0' and 'memory controller 1'.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.17 §1.5 ('connected to two memory controllers that each have a 16-bit LPPDR4X channel'); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.515 Table 15-90 (ddrc_u0_mrr_data, ddrc_u1_mrr_data); external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/utils/mem_controller_utils.c:83-88 (get_ddrc_address: block 1 at +0x1000), :604-607 (ms_write_both_ddrc_reg); external/et-man/ET-SoC Errata.pdf pdf p.88 (errata 5.2 cites the uMCTL2 Databook v3.50a)
note: The datasheet disagrees: 'two 16-bit LPDDR4X physical interfaces sharing a single 32-bit controller' (external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7). Firmware and PRM agree on two controllers; see dram.topo.phy and the ask.

statement: One DDR PHY per memory shire serves both channels: the firmware writes one PHY training message block per memory shire, with the DRAM's MR14 (VREF-DQ) set for 'Channel A' and 'Channel B'; the open RTL gives the memory shire's DDR subsystem 4 data-byte lanes (DBYTEs, 2 per 16-bit channel), 6 address/command blocks (ANIBs) and a 16-bit DRAM data width.
source: external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:190-192 (ms_patch_phy_ram_before_training); external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/utils/mem_controller_utils.c:778-783 (ms_write_phy_ram: one PHY RAM window per memory shire); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:40 (DDR_DRAM_DATA_SIZE 16), :48-49 (DDR_NUM_ANIBS 6, DDR_NUM_DBYTES 4); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.514 (ddrc_reset_ctl 'DDRC PUB reset')
note: The PHY stores up to four PSTATEs of training values (errata 5.4, pdf p.90) and has a PUB: a Synopsys DesignWare LPDDR4-class PHY, product and version not named in any source. core-et is the Erbium-branch open drop; its memory-shire headers match the ET-SoC-1 firmware wherever both speak (see dram.addr.*).

statement: The NoC connects three ports to each memory shire (memory traffic, global-atomic responses, ESR accesses); the memory port is an AXI slave with a 512-bit data path (a whole 64-byte line per beat), and the NoC side delivers at most 32 GB/s per memory shire, almost twice the LPDDR4X side.
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7.1.1 and §7.1.1.1

statement: On the die the memory shires and their LPDDR4X PHYs form a strip about 1.76 mm wide down each side (1.74 and 1.80 mm); the 6-column shire grid between them spans about 22.2 mm.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-27-chip-diagram/facts.json facts['L08'], facts['L09'] (from docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/report.json inputs.memshire_w_mm)
note: Derived from the published die size and photo geometry, not from a floorplan document.

statement: The boot firmware programs the memory PLL in memory shire 0 and memory shire 4 only: one PLL per side.
source: external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:134-172 (configure_memshire_plls: program_memshire_pll(0, ...), program_memshire_pll(4, ...))
note: How the clock reaches memory shires 1-3 and 5-7 is not described; presumably distributed along each side.

statement: The memory shire that serves a line is picked by physical-address bits 8:6, so consecutive 64-byte lines rotate over the eight memory shires; the memory shire's read counter confirmed the bits for 64 of 64 lines in every one of 15 passes on three cards.
source: external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:21 (`MEMSHIRE_SEL_ADDR_RANGE 8:6`); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.26 §1.4.3 ('the Memory Shire is selected by the NoC using bits [8:6] by default'); external/et-platform/device-minion-runtime/tools/zebumem.c:68-72; docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json [item=MEM-P3].per_card.<card>.tests.P3_msmap_match (64 of 64 lines per pass); anatomy page §4
note: Measured as well as specified. PA[8:6] are the low three bits of the L3 home shire's PA[10:6], so memory shire m serves home shires m, m+8, m+16, m+24.

statement: Inside the memory shire, physical-address bit 9 picks the controller (the channel): the memory shire's control register resets with its controller-select bit field at 9 and both controllers enabled, and the default boot never rewrites it. The two channels alternate every 512 bytes.
value: PA[9]
source: external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:22 (`MEMSHIRE_MCTL_SEL_ADDR_RANGE 9`); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/hwinc/ms_regs.h:160 (MS_REGS_MS_MEM_CTL_RESET_VALUE 0x000307f1892481c6: esr_ms_addr_mc_bit_sel = 9, esr_ms_mc_en = 3; fields at ms_regs.h:489-600); external/core-et/rtl/inc/esr_defines.vh:149-158 (ESR_MS_MEM_CTL_RESET_VAL); only the reduced-memory-shire path writes ms_mem_ctl (external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/noc_configuration.c:294-313); zebumem.c:72 ('addr[9] controller (0=even, 1=odd)')
note: Upgrades the earlier inference from a tool comment (counters-and-dram.md §3.4, chip-diagram fact L50): the reset value is in the SoC's own register header. Latency cannot see this bit: flipping it, like flipping a bank bit, lets the second load ride along (memprobe summary.json bits['9'].b_minus_b0_med = 0).

statement: Before a request reaches its controller, the memory shire removes physical-address bits 9:6 (the memory-shire and channel bits), so each controller sees its own lines as one contiguous address space.
value: PA[9:6] removed
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/hwinc/ms_regs.h:160 (reset value decodes to esr_ms_addr_remove_bit_sel0..3 = 6, 7, 8, 9); external/core-et/rtl/inc/esr_defines.vh:149-158; external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_types.vh (memshire_esr_ctl_t)

statement: The controllers' address map as programmed (ECC off): column bits 4:0 = HIF 4:0, bank bits 2:0 = HIF 7:5, column bits 9:5 = HIF 12:8, row bits 16:0 = HIF 29:13 (HIF is the controller's internal address in 16-bit words).
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4639-4654 (ADDRMAP1 0x00030303, ADDRMAP2 0x03000000, ADDRMAP3 0x03030303, ADDRMAP5-6 0x07070707, ADDRMAP7 0x00000f07); field meanings and internal bases from external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/etsoc_hal/inc/DWC_ddr_umctl2.html (ADDRMAP1-7); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md §3.4
note: Register values are from the firmware source; the running cards' registers have not been read back (the hub's ask-memshire). The 32 GB ECC branch (:4590-4626) is not taken: ECC is off.

statement: In physical-address terms, inside one channel: bank = PA[12:10] (8 banks), column = PA[17:13] and PA[5:1] (1,024 columns of 16 bits, a 2 KB page), row = PA[34:18] (17 bits). A 64-byte line is two 32-byte BL16 bursts from one row; PA[5] picks the half.
source: derived from dram.addr.strip and dram.addr.addrmap (HIF = controller byte address / 2 for a 16-bit channel); measured by flipping one bit: docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json bits['13'..'17'].b_minus_b0_med = -12 (same row), bits['18'..'29'] = +9 (other row), bits['6'..'12'] ~ 0; docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json MEM-P4; anatomy page §5 #which-address-bits-share-a-row; docs/research/counters-and-dram.md §3.4
note: Bank and row bits are measured (a same-bank, other-row pair conflicts from bit 18 up on three cards); the split of PA[12:10] into bank rather than channel or column is from the programmed map. zebumem.c:74-111 prints a different swizzle, but only 'if using DDR DRAM models' (an emulation model), and silicon disagrees with it.

statement: Consequences of the map: 64-byte lines rotate over the 8 memory shires, the 2 channels of each alternate every 512 B, a channel sees one line per 1 KB and puts consecutive lines of its own in consecutive banks, a bank's row holds 32 lines spaced 8 KB apart, and a 256 KB aligned block touches one row in each of the 128 channel-banks.
source: docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:352-371 (§3.4); docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md '## Rows' (sequential: next bank, 32 columns per row visit)

statement: DRAM starts at physical address 0x80_0000_0000; minions reach only the 'Low' view, and device allocations come back as 0x80_xxxx_xxxx addresses.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.551 (Table 15-96) and p.553 (Table 15-98); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:348-350, 379

statement: 32 GB of LPDDR4X on the V3 cards (a Micron part): 2 GB, i.e. 16 Gbit, per channel; the chip supports up to 32 GB 'using LPDDR4X at 16 Gbits per channel'.
source: external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf pdf p.1 ('32GB (Micron part) v3 card'); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7.1; external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:389-398 (MR8 density decode to 32 GB)

statement: Each channel is one rank of 8 banks x 131,072 rows x 2 KB pages (1,024 columns of 16 bits): 8 x 131,072 x 2 KB = 2 GB, matching the capacity. One activate therefore senses 16,384 bits into one bank's sense amplifiers.
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4639-4654 (3 bank, 10 column, 17 row address bits); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:38 (`DDR_BANKS_SIZE 3`); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4539 (ODTMAP rank 0 only); JEDEC JESD209-4 addressing for a 16 Gb-per-channel LPDDR4 die (8 banks, R0-R16, C0-C9, 2 KB page)
note: The geometry is what the programmed map and the capacity require and what JEDEC specifies for this density (GENERIC); the part's datasheet, which would confirm it, is not in the sources.

statement: A 64-byte line uses 512 of the 16,384 bits an activate senses: 1/32 of the open row. The other 31 lines of that row (8 KB apart in the address space) can then be read as row hits until the row closes.
source: arithmetic on dram.org.geometry and dram.addr.pa-map

statement: The exact LPDDR4X part (Micron part number), its die density, the number of dies per package and whether each channel is one x16 die or two byte-mode dies are not in any source. The firmware reads the vendor (MR5; Micron = 0xFF) and density (MR8) at every boot and logs them, but no log has been captured.
source: external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf pdf p.1; external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:364-398 (ddr_config: 'DRAM vendor = MICRON', 'DRAM size = 32GB'); external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/utils/mem_controller_utils.c:936-1027 (ms_verify_ddr_density; comment 'for the micron part it is 0x10 for 32gb and 0x18 for 64gb')
note: The firmware labels MR8 density code 6 '64gb/32GB' (mem_controller_utils.c:1000-1004); in JEDEC LPDDR4 terms code 6 is 32 Gb per die, 16 Gb per channel (GENERIC), which fits 2 GB per channel.

statement: The die's internal organisation below the bank (subarrays or mats, cells per bitline, open or folded bitlines, sense-amplifier variant, wordline boost and array voltages, cell capacitance, process node) is vendor-proprietary and appears in no ET source; the diagram's transistor level is therefore JEDEC/textbook GENERIC.
source: none (absence noted across external/et-man, external/core-et, external/et-platform)

statement: The firmware hard-codes the '933 MHz' DDR mode on every card: the controller (DFI) clock is 933 MHz and runs 1:2 with the DRAM clock, so the DRAM clock is 1,866 MHz and the data rate 3,733 MT/s, not the datasheet's 4,266. Telemetry reads mhz.ddr = 933 in every sample.
source: external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:643-649 (DDR_FREQUENCY_933MHZ, '//TODO: decide ddr_mode'); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:768 (DfiFreqRatio_p0=1), :4536 (MSTR 0x00080020: lpddr4=1, burst_rdwr=8 = BL16); docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace2-telemetry.jsonl field mhz.ddr
note: One DFI clock = 1.071 ns, one DRAM clock tCK = 0.536 ns; timings below convert DFI clocks to ns. At 600 MHz one minion cycle is 1.667 ns.

statement: At 3,733 MT/s a 16-bit channel peaks at 7.47 GB/s, a memory shire at 14.9 GB/s and the chip at 119.5 GB/s; at the datasheet's 4,266 MT/s the chip would reach 136.5 GB/s.
source: arithmetic: 2 B x 3.733 GT/s; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.4 §1 (4,266 MT/s, printed '133 Gbytes/s')

statement: Each memory shire's NoC side (32 GB/s) is 2.1x its DRAM side at the programmed rate (14.9 GB/s).
source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7.1.1; dram.ctl.peak-bw

statement: Streaming from DRAM the whole chip reaches 76 GB/s at 600 MHz (64% of 119.5); tensor stores to DRAM also reach 76 GB/s, stores through the L1 27 GB/s.
source: docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'Bandwidth at 600 MHz, 1,024 minions' (E33, E29); docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table rows 'Tensor load from DRAM', 'fsw.ps stores to DRAM through the L1'

statement: Open-page policy: the controller keeps a bank's row open until it must close it (another row of that bank, or a refresh); no page-close timer, no auto-precharge.
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4661-4664 (SCHED 0x00a01f01: pageclose=0; SCHED1 pageclose_timer=0), :4668 (PCCFG 0); external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:245 (config_auto_precharge = 0); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.514 (ddrc_main_ctl: read/write auto-precharge, high/low priority); meaning of pageclose=0 from external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/etsoc_hal/inc/DWC_ddr_umctl2.html (SCHED.pageclose: 'the bank remains open until there is a need to close it ... also known as open page policy')
note: Measured: 96% of loads whose previous load came after the last refresh were row hits, 4% across a refresh (anatomy §5; 95-96% vs 3-4% on three cards).

statement: Activate-to-read delay tRCD = 17 DFI clocks = 18.2 ns (10.9 minion cycles at 600 MHz).
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4430 (DRAMTMG4 0x11040a11: t_rcd=0x11); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:303
note: Measured: an open-row hit saves 11-12 cycles (dram.lat.row-hit).

statement: Precharge time tRP = 17 DFI clocks = 18.2 ns (10.9 cycles).
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4430 (DRAMTMG4 t_rp=0x11); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:304
note: Measured: a load to another row of the bank just used pays about 9-10 cycles more (dram.lat.row-sequential).

statement: Minimum row-open time tRAS = 40 DFI clocks = 42.9 ns; row cycle tRC (activate to activate in one bank) = 59 DFI clocks = 63.2 ns (37.9 cycles).
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4415 (DRAMTMG0 0x1e261f28: t_ras_min=0x28), :4417 (DRAMTMG1 0x0007083b: t_rc=0x3b); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:305-306
note: tRC matches the measured back-to-back row-conflict penalty (+36.5 to +38.5 cycles, dram.lat.row-conflict).

statement: Read latency RL = 18 DFI clocks = 36 DRAM clocks = 19.3 ns (read DBI on); write latency WL = 8 DFI = 16 DRAM clocks = 8.6 ns.
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4425 (DRAMTMG2 0x08121316: read_latency=0x12, write_latency=0x8), :4440 (INIT3 mr=0x64 (MR1), emr=0x36 (MR2)); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:307

statement: Burst length 16 on a 16-bit channel: one READ returns 32 bytes in 8 DRAM clocks (4.3 ns, tCCD = 4 DFI clocks), so a 64-byte line takes two READs to the same row.
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4536 (MSTR burst_rdwr=0x8 = BL16 per external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/etsoc_hal/inc/DWC_ddr_umctl2.html MSTR.burst_rdwr), :4430 (t_ccd=0x4); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:308, 366

statement: Activate-to-activate in different banks tRRD = 10 DFI = 10.7 ns; at most four activates per rolling tFAW = 38 DFI = 40.7 ns per channel.
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4430 (t_rrd=0xa), :4415 (t_faw=0x26); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:309

statement: Write recovery: MR1 = 0x64 sets nWR = 34 DRAM clocks (18.2 ns); write-to-precharge wr2pre = 30 DFI clocks, read-to-precharge rd2pre = 8.
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4440 (INIT3 mr=0x64), :4415 (wr2pre=0x1e), :4417 (rd2pre=0x8); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:310, 322

statement: Data-bus inversion is on for reads and writes, and data masking is enabled (MR3 = 0xF1).
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4522 (DBICTL 0x7: rd_dbi_en=1, wr_dbi_en=1, dm_en=1), :4398 (INIT4 emr2=0xf1 = MR3); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:322

statement: All-bank refresh every tREFI = 113 x 32 = 3,616 DFI clocks = 3.875 us, each taking tRFCab = 262 DFI clocks = 280.7 ns; per-bank refresh off; temperature derating not enabled.
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4441 (RFSHCTL0 0x00210000: per_bank_refresh=0), :4443 (RFSHTMG 0x80710106: t_rfc_nom_x1_x32=0x71, t_rfc_min=0x106), :5475 (RFSHCTL3=0: auto-refresh on after init), :4686-4688 (DERATEEN commented out: 'FUTURE derate is not needed for bring-up'); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/etsoc_hal/inc/DWC_ddr_umctl2.html RFSHTMG.t_rfc_nom_x1_sel ('for ... per-bank refresh only'; unit 'multiples of 32 DFI clock cycles')
note: counters-and-dram.md §3.2 had to guess the x32 reading because t_rfc_nom_x1_sel=1; the uMCTL2 register description says x1_sel applies only to per-bank refresh, and the measured period (dram.lat.refresh-period) confirms x32.

statement: All-bank refresh keeps each channel busy 280.7 / 3,875 ns = 7.2% of the time; 7.2% of loads issued at random phases landed inside a refresh.
source: arithmetic on dram.ctl.refresh-mode; docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json refresh.in_refresh = 0.0721

statement: No power-down and no self-refresh: the firmware disables both 'for performance reasons', so an idle channel stays in active standby with its clocks running.
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:5459 (PWRCTL 0x0), :4738; docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:331
note: GENERIC consequence: the DRAM's active-standby current flows whenever the card is up; its share of the idle 12-18 W unmetered power is unattributed (hub §4.2).

statement: Automatic ZQ calibration (the periodic re-trim of the DRAM's output-driver and termination impedance) is disabled.
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4446 (ZQCTL0 0xc3a50000: dis_auto_zq=1, dis_srx_zqcl=1); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:332

statement: The controller requests DFI controller updates (PHY re-trims) automatically every 64-255 x 1,024 DFI clocks (70-280 us).
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4528-4531 (DFIUPD0 dis_auto_ctrlupd=0; DFIUPD1 interval min 64, max 255 x1024); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:333
note: That these cause rare latency blips is an inference (counters-and-dram.md), not measured.

statement: DRAM ECC is off.
source: external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:643-647 (ddr_mode .ecc = false); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4557 (ECCCFG0 0x003f7f10 'disable ECC')

statement: Each controller has two AXI ports with aging on: port 0 at priority 15 (commented 'lower priority') and port 1 at priority 8 ('higher priority'), for reads and writes alike; the memory shire keeps high/low request lines per controller, and the shire cache marks its to-memory requests high or low QoS from an ESR.
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4670-4680 (PCFGR_0 0x100f, PCFGR_1 0x1008, PCFGW_0 0x100f, PCFGW_1 0x1008); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:95 (`MEMSHIRE_WRITE_CNT_SIZE`, 'one per priority'); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_types.vh (ddrc_esr_ctl_t: u0/u1 csysreq_hi/lo); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.97 §4.1 (esr_sc_axi_qos: AXI_QOS_MEM_HIGH_PRIORITY / _LOW_PRIORITY)
note: Which traffic is steered to which port, and what esr_sc_axi_qos is set to, is not in the sources (ask).

statement: The controller's transaction store (CAM) gives 32 entries to low-priority reads (SCHED.lpr_num_entries = 0x1f, 'this value + 1'); the total depth, a build parameter, is not in the sources.
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4661 (SCHED 0x00a01f01); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/etsoc_hal/inc/DWC_ddr_umctl2.html SCHED.lpr_num_entries description
note: Total CAM depth (MEMC_NO_OF_ENTRY) unknown.

statement: The scheduler serves up to 15 transactions of one kind (high-priority reads, low-priority reads, writes) before switching when another kind waits; low-priority reads and writes may be starved at most 127 clocks, high-priority reads 1.
source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4665-4667 (PERFHPR1 0x0f000001, PERFLPR1 0x0f00007f, PERFWR1 0x0f00007f)
note: Field meanings are the uMCTL2 register names (xact_run_length, max_starve); the scheduler's algorithm itself is Synopsys's and GENERIC here.

statement: The memory shire contains an atomic unit with a small atomic cache (ms_atomic_sm_ctl bits 7:4 flag which entries hold dirty data; a 4-bit state), and the datasheet lists 'LPDDR4X support for global atomic operations'.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.514 Table 15-90 (ms_atomic_sm_ctl); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:121 (`MEMSHIRE_ATOMIC_STATE_SIZE 4`), :268-271 (memshire atomics); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7.1
note: When a global atomic on a DRAM address is done here rather than at the L3 home is not documented (ask).

statement: The memory-shire and DDR-controller registers are reachable only by the service processor.
source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.512 §15.4.3.1; docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:346

statement: Each memory shire has a perf monitor (40-bit cycle counter at 933 MHz and two event counters). The firmware sets them to count mesh reads and writes, which a user kernel can sample through syscall 10; the same monitor can count controller commands (activate, precharge, refresh, per bank), but only M-mode can select that and the encodings are in a document not in the sources.
source: docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:381-418 (§3.5); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:215-250 (MCOP qualifier: cmd bits 14:0, bank bits 27:20; MESHCNT qualifier)
note: Hub rungs 13-14 and the missing 'Memory Shire Specification §5.4.22-29'.

statement: A typical DRAM load, timed one at a time: 299 cycles (500 ns at 600 MHz), the median of 4,500 loads from shire 0 to random lines; 299 in each of 15 passes on three cards.
source: docs/reports/2026-09-19-et-soc1-memory-anatomy.html headline tile 'A DRAM load, typical' (19 Sep: 4,500 loads; 26 Sep: 15 passes on three cards)

statement: A DRAM pointer chase: 296.6-297.1 cycles from shires 0 and 31, 287.2-288.8 from shires 7 and 24 (479-495 ns at 600 MHz), in every pass on every card.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/lat.json items[LAT-M2].per_card.<card>.passes[].DRAM; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'L3 and DRAM latency by requesting shire' (E36)
note: About 490 ns, a fifth more than an A100's HBM (405 ns).

statement: At 800 MHz the chase reads 352-368 cycles (440-460 ns): the mesh and DDR parts do not scale with the minion clock; fitted, a DRAM load is 86.3 minion cycles + 344.8 ns.
source: docs/findings/05-claims.md, rows 'DRAM' and 'Latency models' (E33)

statement: Whole DRAM load = 110 + 12 x hops(requester -> L3 home) + 91 + 12 x hops(L3 home -> memory shire) cycles; left as fitted on aifoundry2, within +-3 cycles for 97.0% of lines on aifoundry2, 92.9% on aifoundry3, 94.4% on aifoundry1-c1.
source: anatomy page §4 (formula); docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DRAM latency against the 19 September model' (E35, docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json MEM-P2)
note: Refitted pass by pass the constant reads 90-91 on all three cards (docs/reports/data/2026-09-26-memprobe-3cards/cards.json ms_const).

statement: With the memory shires one hop outside the grid, the memory shire's position adds 12-84 cycles (1-7 hops from the L3 home, 2.6 on average).
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-27-chip-diagram/facts.json facts['L44']; anatomy page §1

statement: Of the 91-cycle memory-shire leg (152 ns), about 28 cycles are the DRAM's own timing: the activate (tRCD, 11 cycles) and the read latency plus two 32-byte bursts (19.3 + 8.6 ns, 17 cycles). At most about 63 cycles (~105 ns) are the memory shire itself: queues, controller, PHY and clock crossings.
source: anatomy page §4 ('Of the 91 cycles (152 ns), the DRAM chip itself accounts for about 28'); dram.ctl.tRCD, dram.ctl.RL-WL, dram.ctl.burst
note: 'At most' because each hop further out that the memory shires might sit moves 12 cycles from the constant into the mesh legs.

statement: How the memory shire's ~63 cycles split between the NoC AXI port and clock crossing, the address strip, the controller's port, CAM and scheduler, the DFI and the PHY's transmit and receive paths is not known.
source: none: no memory-shire description is in the sources (hub ask 'ask-memshire', docs/reports/sources/limits-of-observability.data.json improvements[25])

statement: A load that finds its row open skips the activate and saves 11-12 cycles (about 19 ns, tRCD): 215 against 226 cycles in the refresh series; the two clusters' means were 11.0-11.6 cycles apart on three cards.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json refresh.open_med = 214, refresh.closed_med = 226, refresh.closed_minus_open = 11.6; anatomy page §5 #refresh-caught-in-the-act; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DRAM refresh and open rows' (E35)
note: The registered three-card test read 5.3-6.6 cycles because it missed the later build's 7-cycle timer offset; re-referenced to each pass's own L1 hit it reads 11.0-11.6 (anatomy page, 'Checked on three cards').

statement: Two loads to the same bank but different rows, issued together: the second pays about +37 cycles (36.9 on aifoundry2, 37.4 on aifoundry3, 36.5 on aifoundry1-c1; 38.5 on 19 September): it cannot activate its row until tRC (63.2 ns = 37.9 cycles) after the first activate.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json [item=MEM-P4].per_card.<card>.tests.P4_row_conflict_extra; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DRAM bank timing (bits)' (E35); anatomy page §5
note: The tRC explanation is et-derived: the penalty matches the programmed tRC within a cycle.

statement: Issued one after the other: a second load to another row of the same bank pays about +9-10 cycles (the precharge, tRP = 11 cycles), one to the same row saves 11-12, one to another bank costs nothing extra.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json bits['18'..'29'].b_minus_b0_med = 9, bits['13'..'17'] = -12; docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json MEM-P4 P4_seq_row, P4_seq_col, P4_seq_bank (+10, -11, 0 on every card)

statement: Every load of the latency decomposition found its row closed: each came 2,600 cycles or more after its row was last opened, longer than a refresh period; after up to 27 ms idle a DRAM load is 10.5 cycles slower, the row closure, and no other wake-up cost.
source: anatomy page §4 ('Every one of these loads found its row closed'); docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'No array wake-up latency' (E18)

statement: Folding 19,000 DRAM load times on their timestamps shows refresh every 2,325.4 cycles = 3.876 us on every card (15 passes); a load that arrives during a refresh waits up to 208 extra cycles (347 ns), and refresh closes the open row.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json refresh.period_cycles = 2325.4, refresh.max_wait = 208; docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json [item=MEM-P5].per_card.<card>.tests.P5_refresh_period, .P5_max_extra; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DRAM refresh and open rows' (E35)
note: Matches the programmed tREFI (3.875 us) to 0.02%. The 208-cycle wait is 347 ns against tRFCab 280.7 ns; the remaining ~66 ns is not attributed (a precharge-all before the refresh and the re-activate after it are the GENERIC candidates).

statement: A row stays open until a refresh or a conflicting load closes it; no idle timer was seen: in the refresh series 96% of loads with no refresh since the previous one were row hits (3,556 of 3,713, after 450-2,000 idle cycles), 4% across a refresh.
unit: % row hits without a refresh between
source: anatomy page §5 #how-long-a-row-stays-open; docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json refresh.rowlife

statement: The DRAM leg starts when the L3 home's cache bank misses: the L3 miss costs 42 shire clocks (idle, excluding NoC and memory) and the bank sends the read through its 512-bit To_Sys port into the NoC.
source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.11 Table 1 ('L3 cache read miss 42 + NoC & Mem latency'), pdf p.8 ('it uses its 512b To_Sys port into the NoC to make the request to the memory'), pdf p.55 (misses and victims to the to_sys port)

statement: Reading DRAM costs 114.6 pJ per byte above idle [89.0-141.3 over 18 passes] with 1 KB tensor loads at 600 MHz (aifoundry2 111.5, aifoundry3 105.6, aifoundry1-c1 126.6): about 7.3 nJ per 64-byte line.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json reruns.levels_pj_per_byte['dram'] (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table row 'DRAM'

statement: Even DRAM is data-dependent: a tensor load from DRAM costs 94.6 pJ/B on zeros [86.2-105.7] and 132.6 on random data [117.9-145.4]; a tensor store 94.4 and 141.9.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json catalogue.combined['tload/dram/zeros'], ['tload/dram/random'], ['tstore/dram/zeros'], ['tstore/dram/random']; docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table rows
note: With read and write DBI on and LVSTL I/O terminated to ground (GENERIC), driving ones costs current and zeros almost none; that is one plausible share of the gap, not measured separately.

statement: Stores to DRAM through the L1 write-back path (fsw.ps) cost 341.5 pJ/B on random data at 27 GB/s: each store allocates its line, so the byte pays a DRAM read and a DRAM write.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json catalogue.combined['st_stream/dram/random']; docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table row 'fsw.ps stores to DRAM through the L1'

statement: A tensor store to DRAM is not distinguishable from a tensor load in energy on any card (+8.4, +7.3 and +14.5 pJ/B, 99% intervals all including 0).
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/cat.json [item=CAT-e].per_card.<card>.tstore_minus_tload; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'A tensor store to DRAM against a tensor load, random' (E45)

statement: About 70% of a DRAM byte's energy lands on no metered rail: a DRAM tensor load splits 2% minion cores, 11% SRAM, 18% mesh, 69% unmetered; the fit of the unmetered remainder puts 72.7 (aifoundry2), 72.7 (aifoundry3) and 81.6 (aifoundry1-c1) pJ per DRAM byte in the DDR PHY, the I/O rail and the DRAM chips.
source: docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md rail-split table row 'DRAM, tensor load' and unmetered-fit table row 'per DRAM byte'; docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json unmetered.<card>.coef.dram_pj_per_byte; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'Rail split, DRAM read'

statement: How the ~73 pJ/B off-rail DRAM energy splits between the memory shires' logic, the PHY's I/O, the DRAM core (activate, sensing, column path) and the DRAM's own I/O is not measurable on the card: none of those rails has a current sensor.
source: docs/findings/19-observability-and-the-unmetered.md ('The other rails — DDR core 0.8 V, VDDQ 1.1 V, VDDQLP ... have set points in the PMIC and no telemetry'); docs/research/power-telemetry.md:47-52, 255

statement: The DRAM row pattern does not change the energy per byte: row hits 155.9, row misses 158.5, sequential 156.4 pJ/B on random data (120.4 / 118.5 / 120.6 on zeros), indistinguishable on every card; an activation costing 30 pJ/B on zeros or 50 on random data would have shown.
source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json catalogue.combined['dramrow2/rowhit/random'], ['dramrow2/rowmiss/random'], ['dramrow2/seq/random'] (and /zeros); docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md '## Rows: does the DRAM row pattern matter?'; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DRAM row walks (seq, rowhit, rowmiss) over a DRAM tensor load' (E45)
note: The manual's caveat: with 32 streams interleaved and a refresh every 2,325 cycles, every pattern may have paid an activation; so the activate energy is bounded, not measured. Per 64-byte line the bound is ~1.9 nJ (zeros) to ~3.2 nJ (random).

statement: A random 4-byte element gathered from DRAM costs 9.8 nJ (a whole line fetched for 4 bytes), at 1.19 G elements/s chip-wide; a scatter into DRAM 23.8 nJ at 0.42 G/s.
source: docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table rows 'DRAM' (gathers and scatters); docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/gs.json items['GS-RATE'].pooled

statement: DRAM is 30x the energy of the shire's own scratchpad per byte read and 17x per byte written; relaying a result through DRAM costs 12.9-13.1x handing it to the next shire.
source: docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md ('DRAM is 30x the energy ...'); docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'The relay (V3)' (E29)

statement: Three card rails serve the memory path: VDD_DDR (the memory shires, 0.8 V set point, 875 mV in the card's power-tree figure), VDD_QLP (the LPDDR4X I/O VDDQ; 640 mV set point read on aifoundry2, 620 mV in the figure) and VDD_Q (1.1 V: the LPDDR4X's VDDQ/VDD2 core supply, as the figure labels it). None reports current.
source: docs/research/power-telemetry.md:47-52 (from the power-tree images, external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf pdf pp.2-4); docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace2-telemetry.jsonl fields reg_mv.ddr = 800, reg_mv.vddqlp = 640, reg_mv.vddq = 1100
note: JEDEC LPDDR4X (GENERIC): VDD1 1.8 V, VDD2 1.1 V, VDDQ 0.6 V. Which card rail feeds the DRAM's VDD1 is not in the sources.

statement: The memory shires' own voltage monitors read the 0.8 V DDR rail at 767-768 mV at idle, and it droops 0.86-1.01 mV per watt of off-rail DRAM power (1 mV ~ 1.2 W of DRAM): a proxy DRAM meter, refreshed every service-processor pass.
source: docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DDR rail droop per off-rail DRAM watt' (E30, E46); docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md 'A droop meter for DRAM'; horace2-telemetry.jsonl die_mv.ddr

statement: A DRAM bit is one 1T1C cell: an NMOS access transistor whose gate is the wordline and whose drain is the bitline, in series with a storage capacitor; the stored charge is the bit, it leaks away (hence refresh), and reading it is destructive until the sense amplifier restores it.
source: GENERIC (textbook DRAM; no ET source describes the die)

statement: Between accesses each bitline pair is held at half the array voltage by a precharge/equalize circuit (typically three NMOS: two tie BL and /BL to the half-voltage, one shorts them together); the equalize signal turns off just before a wordline rises.
source: GENERIC (textbook DRAM)

statement: Activate: the row address is decoded, and the selected (sub-)wordline driver pulls its wordline up to a boosted voltage above the array voltage, so every access NMOS on that row turns fully on and passes a full level.
source: GENERIC (textbook DRAM)

statement: Each cell shares its charge with its bitline, nudging it slightly above or below the half-voltage; the bitline sense amplifier, a cross-coupled latch of two NMOS and two PMOS, is then fired (NMOS side pulled to ground, PMOS side to the array voltage) and drives the pair to full rail, which also rewrites the cell. The row of latched sense amplifiers is the open page ('row buffer').
source: GENERIC (textbook DRAM)
note: On the ET-SoC-1's channels one activate latches 16,384 bits (dram.org.geometry).

statement: Read: the column decoder raises a column-select line, turning on column-select NMOS pairs that connect the chosen sense amplifiers to local and then global I/O lines, where secondary sense amplifiers pick up the data; LPDDR4 fetches 16 bits per DQ per READ (16n prefetch), 256 bits for a x16 channel, and serialises them 16:1 onto each pin.
source: GENERIC (JEDEC JESD209-4 LPDDR4 16n prefetch; array circuit textbook)

statement: LPDDR4X signals use LVSTL: each DQ driver pulls up to a 0.6 V VDDQ or down to ground, and the receiver terminates to ground, so a driven 1 draws current through the termination and a 0 almost none; DBI inverts a byte that holds more than four ones. (LPDDR4's LVSTL pull-up is usually an NMOS, N-over-N; the transistor choice is the vendor's.)
source: GENERIC (JEDEC LPDDR4/LPDDR4X)
note: ET has read and write DBI on (dram.ctl.dbi); the card's VDD_QLP set point is 620-640 mV (dram.pwr.rails).

statement: Precharge: the wordline falls (access transistors off, the restored cells isolated), the sense amplifiers are disabled and the equalizers turn back on, returning every bitline pair to the half-voltage for the next activate.
source: GENERIC (textbook DRAM)

statement: LPDDR4 commands travel on a 6-bit single-data-rate command/address bus: an ACTIVATE is two 2-clock parts (ACT-1, ACT-2), a READ or WRITE is RD-1/WR-1 plus CAS-2 (4 clocks), a PRECHARGE 2 clocks.
source: GENERIC (JEDEC JESD209-4)

statement: All-bank refresh: the die's internal counter supplies the row addresses and each REFab activates and precharges a batch of rows in every bank at once; JEDEC LPDDR4 asks for 8,192 refresh commands per 32 ms retention window at normal temperature, which with 131,072 rows per bank means 16 rows of each bank per REFab.
source: GENERIC (JEDEC JESD209-4 tREFW 32 ms, 8,192 REF); rows per bank from dram.org.geometry
note: ET's tREFI 3.875 us is slightly shorter than JEDEC's 3.904 us, so 8,192 refreshes take 31.7 ms.

statement: LPDDR4 needs refresh 2x or 4x as often above 85 C, signalled in its MR4 register. The ET firmware leaves derating off, so refresh stays at 3.875 us whatever the DRAM temperature; nothing in the sources reads the DRAM's temperature.
source: GENERIC (JEDEC JESD209-4 MR4 refresh-rate field); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4686-4688 (DERATEEN commented out)
note: Whether the packages stay under 85 C under load is an ask; the die itself idles at 72 C and reaches 80-90 C under load on these cards.

statement: The programmed timings sit at JEDEC LPDDR4 minimums for a 16 Gb-per-channel die at 3,733 MT/s: tRCD and tRPpb 18 ns, tRAS 42 ns, tRRD 10 ns, tFAW 40 ns, tRFCab 280 ns, RL 36 with read DBI, WL 16, nWR 34, tREFI 3.9 us.
source: GENERIC comparison: values quoted from JEDEC JESD209-4 from memory of the standard, not from an ET source; ET values from dram.ctl.*
note: tRFCab = 280 ns is the JEDEC value for 12-16 Gb per channel, a cross-check on the die density.

statement: A store reaches DRAM only when its dirty line leaves the L3: the L3 bank sends the victim as a write through its To_Sys port to the memory shire PA[8:6] names; the controller queues it in its write store and drains writes in runs of up to 15.
source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.8 (L3 evicts via To_Sys), p.55 (misses and victims to the to_sys port), pp.79-83 (Flush/FlushToMem); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4667 (PERFWR1)

statement: The line comes back the way the request went: the memory shire answers the L3 home over the mesh, the L3 installs it and returns it to the requester; the latency model counts 12 cycles per hop on both legs.
source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.54-55 (misses to to_sys; data returned and installed), p.8; anatomy page §4 (model)

statement: The L3 home misses and sends a 64-byte read with its QoS over the 512-bit To_Sys port.
